meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: How Munib Tracker handles your data: guest data stays on your device, optional sync, the encrypted vault, family circles, location, Qur'an practice audio and analytics.

title: Privacy Policy
intro: {appName} is built to protect your privacy. Your worship data belongs to you.

whoWeAre.heading: Who we are
whoWeAre.body: {appName} is provided by {author}. This policy covers the mobile and web product app and this marketing website ( <nowrap>munibtracker.app</nowrap>). Questions: use our <contact>contact form</contact>.

device.heading: Data stored on your device
device.body: By default, all of your tracking and learning data stays on your device. That includes Salah logs, Zikr and tasbeeh counts, Qaza and fasting records, Qur'an and hadith bookmarks, ayah notes and highlights, reading progress, favorites, custom adhkar, khushu' journal entries, preferences (theme, language, fonts, notifications, home layout, madhhab, Hijri adjustment), and optional PIN lock settings. Guest mode works fully without an account. The weekly coach works out its suggestions on your device from these records with simple rules; nothing is sent to a server or to an AI service to do it.

location.heading: Location
location.body: If you allow location access (or choose a city), Salah times and the Qibla direction are calculated on your device. To show a place name for your coordinates, the app may look it up with BigDataCloud's reverse-geocoding service; searching for a city uses Open-Meteo's geocoding service. Coordinates are not sold and are not required for core tracking. Optional weather overlays may request local conditions from Open-Meteo or MET Norway using your location when that feature is enabled. If you turn on cloud sync, the saved location is sent rounded to about 1 km; your exact coordinates stay on your device.

microphone.heading: Microphone & Qur'an practice
microphone.body: The app uses the microphone only when you turn it on: to dictate custom adhkar, in Qur'an practice and recite-along (including the al-Fatihah check and kids mode) to follow your recitation, for the Verse Detector and recite-to-find, and for hands-free tasbeeh and guided adhkar, which listen for the pauses between the phrases you say or, if you teach a zikr, for repeats of that zikr. Audio is processed on your device. It is not recorded, stored, or uploaded, and practice keeps only counts (for example how many words matched) and ayah numbers — never audio or a transcript. If you teach hands-free tasbeeh a zikr, a short voice pattern (numbers, not a recording) stays on your device only, until you forget it in Settings or reset the app.
microphone.listener: The practice listener is an optional download (about 70 MB). The iOS and Android apps fetch it from the Tilawa project's release host on GitHub; the web app serves an unmodified copy of the same files from its own site. The optional pronunciation listener is downloaded from Quran Lab only after you agree on its consent sheet. Its model is encrypted for your device and runs on the device; setting it up needs a connection, and Quran Lab's SDK renews its permission in the background when you are online. Quran Lab's SDK always sends Quran Lab anonymous daily counts (for example minutes practised and how the model ran) and error reports — never audio, words, names or device identifiers; the app cannot turn these off. After a few practice sessions Quran Lab's own sheet may ask, at most three times, whether you would like to share recordings to improve its free models. Nothing is shared unless you say yes there, and you can turn sharing off and delete what you shared from Settings → Qur'an practice. This applies to every profile, including kids mode, so a parent may want to review it with a child. The listeners are practice aids, not a ruling on your recitation.
microphone.pronunciation: The pronunciation check uses a second on-device speech model. On the web its files are downloaded from a public mirror on Hugging Face and checked against pinned fingerprints. Audio is never saved or uploaded and no cloud speech service is used. Tajweed coaching keeps only which sounds you practised, when, and references to example words — never audio or a score.

masjid.heading: Masjid finder & Umrah mode
masjid.body: To list masjids near you, the app sends our server only a short area code for a cell of about 5 km, never your exact coordinates. The request carries no account, user ID or cookie. Our server looks the area up on OpenStreetMap, caches the public results and sends them back; distances to each masjid are worked out on your device. The server does not log the area you looked up. Your home masjid is saved in your preferences, and iqamah times you type in for it stay on your device and your own synced devices: they are never sent to the Masjid finder or shown to other users. If you mark a Salah as prayed at the masjid, that note is part of your own Salah log. Umrah mode's miqat check uses your location on the device while the screen is open.
masjid.timetable: If you scan your masjid's timetable, the photo is read on your device (Apple Vision on iPhone, ML Kit on Android, or a text-recognition engine that runs inside your browser on the web, downloaded once from a public CDN). The photo and the recognised text are never uploaded; the app's copy of the photo is deleted after reading, or when you finish checking if you choose to keep it on screen. Only the times you review and save are kept, as your private times.

focusLock.heading: Salah focus lock
focusLock.body: The Salah focus lock is optional. If you turn it on, the apps you choose to pause stay on your device. On iPhone they are kept by Apple's Screen Time framework as private tokens we cannot read. On Android the app checks which app is open (using usage access) only while one of your prayer windows is running, and never stores or sends that information. Your focus-lock settings (which prayers, timing and mode) sync with your account like other preferences; your app choices and emergency-unlock history do not.

vault.heading: Private vault: muhasabah, family ties, debts & will
vault.body: Your nightly muhasabah, family-ties list (including the names and phone numbers of relatives you add), debts and trusts record, and Islamic will are kept in an encrypted vault on your device (AES-256-GCM, with the key held in your device's secure storage, or as a browser key that can't be exported on the web). They are not synced unless you turn on vault sync.
vault.excused: Your excused periods (hayd, nifas, illness or travel, and the reason on each excused day) and your khushu' journal follow the same rule: they stay on your device, and they sync only through end-to-end encrypted vault sync. A synced Salah log shows only that a day was excused, never why.
vault.sync: Vault sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted. You choose a passphrase and receive a 24-word recovery code that is shown only once. The encryption key is derived on your device and never sent, so our server stores only encrypted data that we cannot read. If you lose both your passphrase and your recovery code, the synced copy cannot be recovered by anyone, including us; the records on your device keep working.
vault.reminders: Reminders for these records use generic text: lock-screen notifications never show names, amounts or personal reflections. A document photo you attach to a debt is encrypted on your device and is never synced or included in backups. A will or debts statement you export as a PDF is created only to hand to the share or print sheet and is deleted afterwards on iPhone and Android; once you share it, that copy is under your control.

circles.heading: Family circles, partners & group khatm
circles.body: Family circles and accountability partners need a free account, because members see shared progress through our server. A group khatm can also be joined as a guest on the web. Each circle stores only a small, fixed signal: a child's five fard Salah statuses (done or not) and generic rest days, for their parents; a daily "done" for an accountability partner (never your goal or what you missed); and which khatm part each member is reading and when it is done. The server rejects any other field, so your notes, Qaza, journals and goals can't be shared through a circle. A parent's own Salah is never shared, and adults in a family share nothing unless they turn sharing on.
circles.members: Members see the display name you choose for each circle, never your account name or email. A partner's dua or reminder nudge is anonymous. Daily signals are deleted after 90 days and nudges after 30 days. When you leave a circle, you are hidden at once and your signals and membership are deleted after 30 days. Deleting your account removes your circle data; circles you own pass to another member or are dissolved.

notifications.heading: Notifications
notifications.body: Prayer, preferred-time, adhkar, Qaza, fasting, family-ties, muhasabah, iqamah, debt and will, weekly coach, daily content, Friday, Qur'an revision, and achievement reminders are scheduled locally on your device when you enable them. If you allow notifications, the app registers a push token with our server so we can send service announcements, Live Activity updates on iOS, and web push reminders; you can turn these off at any time. Notification content is generated from your preferences and local data. You can disable any category or revoke system permission at any time.
notifications.circles: If you are signed in and belong to a circle, our server can also push three kinds of circle event: a khatm part was completed, a khatm was completed, and someone made dua for you. Their text is fixed and contains no names, circle names, intentions or Salah status. Parents in a family circle can also get a weekly family digest with counts only (for example how many Salah were logged that week), never children's names or individual prayers. Each kind has its own switch in Settings, and the server follows your choice once your preferences have synced. Guests in a group khatm don't receive circle pushes.

account.heading: Optional account & cloud sync
account.body: If you sign in with Google, Apple or Facebook, we store the minimum needed to sync across devices: an account identifier, email and display name from the provider (when provided), and the worship and learning records you choose to sync (for example prayer logs, zikr progress, Qaza, preferences, favorites, bookmarks, ayah notes and highlights, khatm/hifz, custom adhkar, and learning progress). Vault records, your excused periods and your khushu' journal sync only end-to-end encrypted, as described above. We do not sell your data or use it for advertising.

appLock.heading: App lock (PIN & biometrics)
appLock.body: On supported native builds you may enable a PIN and optional device biometrics to unlock the app. The PIN is stored only on your device; biometric checks use the platform secure enclave / keystore. We never receive your PIN or biometric templates.

backups.heading: Backups, import & offline downloads
backups.body: You can export a local JSON backup and restore it later, import Salah history from CSV or JSON, and download optional Qur'an editions, mushaf fonts, hadith collections, or audio for offline use. Exports you share leave your device under your control. Cached downloads stay on-device until you clear them.

reports.heading: Content reports
reports.body: If you report a content error from the app, we receive the details you submit (and any optional attachments) so we can investigate and correct the material. Use reports only for genuine accuracy issues.

thirdParty.heading: Third-party services
thirdParty.body: Depending on features you use, the app or site may contact: our API host for auth and sync; Google, Apple or Facebook for sign-in; Sentry for crash reports (without your worship data); open CDNs for optional Qur'an/hadith/audio content, a public GitHub copy of the Quranic Arabic Corpus for root-word search, a public Hugging Face mirror for speech-model files on the web, and a public CDN for the in-browser timetable reader (see <credits>Credits</credits>); OpenStreetMap, through our server, for the Masjid finder; and weather providers when overlays are enabled. The product app does not embed third-party advertising or behavioural-tracking SDKs.

website.heading: This marketing website
website.body: If Google Analytics 4 is configured for this site, we may collect anonymized page-view and interaction metrics (IP anonymization enabled) to understand how the marketing pages are used. Analytics storage is gated by Google Consent Mode v2 and our first-party cookie banner — defaults deny storage until you accept analytics (or reopen Cookie preferences from the footer). The contact form stores your name, email, and message in our database so our support team can respond; we use it only to reply and do not sell contact data. Analytics on this website is separate from the product app and is not used to profile your worship data.

children.heading: Children
children.body: Kids mode is for children under 13 and is set up by a parent, who confirms their consent in the app; we record when consent was given and which version of this policy it applied to. A child profile holds only a nickname, a birth year and an optional built-in avatar, with no email or password. A child's device is linked with a one-time QR code that expires after five minutes, and the parent can unlink it at any time. The app has no ads or analytics SDKs, and in a child session crash reports carry no user, request or activity details. Parents see only their child's five fard Salah statuses and the stickers earned from them.
children.deletion: Deleting a child profile deletes it and its signals immediately. When a child is ready to move to their own account, the profile and its signals are deleted and the young person joins with sharing off. If the parent who gave consent deletes their account, the child's profile passes to another parent in the family, who must confirm consent again within 30 days or the profile is deleted; with no other parent it is deleted at once. To delete a child profile, remove it from your family circle or contact us.

retention.heading: Retention & deletion
retention.body: Local data remains until you clear app storage, restore a backup, or uninstall. Synced server records are retained while your account exists. You can delete synced data or your account from the app profile; deletion removes your synced records from our servers. Local copies on other devices may remain until you clear them.

transfers.heading: International transfers
transfers.body: Our API and hosting may process data in regions where our cloud providers operate. By signing in and syncing, you understand your account and synced records may be stored outside your country of residence, subject to applicable law.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: We may update this policy as the product evolves. The effective date above will change when we do. Continued use after an update constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Privacy questions: <contact>contact form</contact> or the support / report flows inside the app.
